title: Agatu Chairman Leads SEMA, IOM and Red Cross in Assessment of 32 Flood-Affected Communities
summary: Agatu LGA Chairman Hon. Amb. James Melvin Ejeh appeals for urgent humanitarian assistance following a joint assessment of 32 flood-affected communities, alongside the distribution of 150 life jackets supplied by HYPPADEC.
content:
The Executive Chairman of Agatu Local Government Area, Hon. Amb. James Melvin Ejeh, has appealed for urgent humanitarian assistance for 32 communities reportedly affected by flooding. The appeal was made on Sunday, October 18, 2026, when the Chairman received a joint rapid assessment team from the Benue State Emergency Management Agency (Benue-SEMA), the International Organization for Migration (IOM), and the Nigerian Red Cross.

The team visited to assess the impact of the flooding, identify urgent needs, and help guide possible humanitarian interventions. The Chairman received the delegation alongside the community leaders of Oweto and Utugolugu, Chief Ibrahim Kwelono and Chief Sule Ajaka.

Reports indicated that houses, farmlands, food supplies, and household items had been damaged. These losses have raised concerns about shelter, food security, and the livelihoods of affected residents.

As part of efforts to improve water safety, the Chairman distributed 150 life jackets supplied by HYPPADEC to major boat points, including Oweto, Adana, Abugbe, and other locations. He commended HYPPADEC for its support and urged boat operators and passengers to obey water-safety rules and wear life jackets while travelling by water.

The Chairman appealed to the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), Benue-SEMA, relevant government agencies, humanitarian organisations, and development partners to provide urgent assistance. Priority needs include relief supplies, food, shelter, medical assistance, and livelihood support for affected households.

He was accompanied by nine ward councillors led by the Agatu Legislative Council Leader, Hon. Tony Simon, as well as the Supervisory Councillor for Revenue, Hon. Danjuma Isah Halidu, and other council officials.

The assessment was coordinated by the Executive Secretary of Benue-SEMA, Sir James Aondoakaa Iorpuu, PhD. The team was led by Mr. Orseer Zege, Programme Manager for IDP Operations, who represented the Executive Secretary alongside representatives of IOM and the Nigerian Red Cross.

Mr. Zege expressed sympathy with the affected communities and explained that the assessment findings would help establish the extent of the damage and guide intervention efforts. He added that Benue-SEMA was working with relevant agencies and development partners to facilitate assistance.

The visit highlighted the urgent needs of flood-affected riverine communities and the importance of coordinated humanitarian support, community cooperation, and safe water transportation.
author: Agatu LGA Media Office
